topic.source_contract: Environmental Impact Assessment screening, scoping and Environmental Statement evidence

facts.law: Town and Country Planning EIA Regulations 2017
facts.guard: EIA procedure is not planning permission

facts.instrument: Town and Country Planning (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 2017
facts.guard: regulation scope must be matched to project type and date

facts.scope: NSIP EIA pre-application and Rochdale Envelope
facts.guard: NSIP advice is not a screening or DCO outcome
SEA and project EIA are distinct assessment regimes

facts.scope: agricultural EIA inspections for uncultivated or semi-natural land
facts.guard: agricultural screening is not town-planning EIA permission

scope_guards: Schedule 1 and Schedule 2 development remain distinct; Schedule 2 requires project-specific significant-effects screening.
Indicative thresholds do not create automatic positive or negative screening outcomes.
A screening opinion, scoping opinion and Environmental Statement are separate documents and stages.
An Environmental Statement reports likely significant effects and does not grant planning permission.
Project EIA, Strategic Environmental Assessment and Habitats Regulations Assessment remain distinct.
Town-planning EIA, NSIP EIA and agricultural EIA routes must not be silently merged.
Mitigation, monitoring and alternatives require proposal-specific evidence and decision conditions.
No score or promotion is written without exact project description, screening, scoping, statement, consultation and decision evidence.
